title: Relative pseudo-coherence survives flat base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S^{\prime}\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $f$ locally of finite type [def-pc-morphism-conventions] and $g$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Set $X^{\prime}=X\times_S S^{\prime}$, with projections $q:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every integer $m$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] which is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex], the derived pullback $Lq^*E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S^{\prime}$ with respect to $f^{\prime}$. In particular, if $E$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$, then $Lq^*E$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S^{\prime}$. There is no quasi-coherence hypothesis on $E$ and no Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09UR, lemma-base-change-relative-pseudo-coherent, flat-base-change specialization (flatness implies Tor independence).

proof.text: Fix $m$. Choose the witnesses in [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]: affine opens $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ covering $S$, affine opens $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{ab}$ covering $f^{-1}(V_a)$, and closed embeddings $i_{ab}:U_{ab}\hookrightarrow P_{ab}=\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V_a}$ such that $K_{ab}=R(i_{ab})_*(E|_{U_{ab}})$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], take the covering of each open $g^{-1}(V_a)$ by all its affine opens $W_{ac}=\operatorname{Spec}A^{\prime}_{ac}$. Put $U^{\prime}_{abc}=U_{ab}\times_{V_a}W_{ac}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], these are open subschemes of $X^{\prime}$; for fixed $a,c$ they cover $(f^{\prime})^{-1}(W_{ac})$, since the $U_{ab}$ cover $f^{-1}(V_a)$. They are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with ring $B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}A^{\prime}_{ac}$. All covers may be infinite.

source.place: Tag 09UR, lemma-base-change-relative-pseudo-coherent, first two sentences of proof; Tag 09UI, definition-relative-pseudo-coherence, clause (1).

proof.text: Base change gives $P^{\prime}_{abc}=P_{ab}\times_{V_a}W_{ac}\cong\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{W_{ac}}$: this is the associativity of the fibre-product definition of relative affine space [def-nagata-relative-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $h_{abc}:P^{\prime}_{abc}\to P_{ab}$ and $q_{abc}:U^{\prime}_{abc}\to U_{ab}$ for the projections. The induced $i^{\prime}_{abc}:U^{\prime}_{abc}\to P^{\prime}_{abc}$ is the base change of $i_{ab}$, hence is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The map $W_{ac}\to V_a$ is flat: its local ring maps are those of $g$ at the same points [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus $h_{abc}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Finally, $f^{\prime}$ is locally of finite type: the closed embedding $i_{ab}$ expresses $B_{ab}$ as a quotient of $A_a[T_1,\ldots,T_{n_{ab}}]$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the tensors in step 1 are generated over $A^{\prime}_{ac}$ by the images of those generators. For any affine open $H=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset S^{\prime}$, cover $H$ by principal opens $D(t)\subset H\cap g^{-1}(V_a)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. They are affine with ring $C_t$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme], hence occur among the $W_{ac}$. Above each, the rings $B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}C_t$ are generated over $C$ by $1/t$ and the finitely many polynomial generator images. These affine source opens cover $(f^{\prime})^{-1}(H)$, proving the condition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 09UR, base-changed polynomial embedding; morphisms.tex Tags 01QR (closed immersion base change) and 01U9 (flat base change).

proof.text:
Let $E^{\prime}=Lq^*E$ and $F_{abc}=E|_{U_{ab}}$. If $j:U_{ab}\to X$ and $j^{\prime}:U^{\prime}_{abc}\to X^{\prime}$ are the open inclusions, then $q\circ j^{\prime}=j\circ q_{abc}$. Applying [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] to these two factorizations gives $(E^{\prime})|_{U^{\prime}_{abc}}\cong Lq_{abc}^*F_{abc}$. By [lem-sc-flat-pullback-tor-independent] applied to the flat $h_{abc}$ of step 2 and to $i_{ab}$, higher Tor of their source stalk rings over the ambient stalk vanishes. [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] exchanges the two factors, giving exactly the order in the stalkwise Tor-independence hypothesis of [lem-sfb-tor-independent-closed-pushforward-comparison]. Apply that node to this Cartesian square and $F_{abc}$; $i_{ab}$ is a closed immersion by construction. The resulting derived-category isomorphism is
$$R(i^{\prime}_{abc})_*((E^{\prime})|_{U^{\prime}_{abc}})\cong Lh_{abc}^*K_{ab}.$$
The exchange statement allows arbitrary complexes, so no quasi-coherence or boundedness has been imposed on $E$.

source.place: Tag 09UR, displayed base-change isomorphism and its stalk calculation; perfect.tex Tag 0E23, lemma-compare-base-change-closed-immersion.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-derived-pullback-m-pseudocoherent], the right side in step 3 is $m$-pseudo-coherent, because $K_{ab}$ is. The left side is therefore $m$-pseudo-coherent as well: in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex], compose each local strictly perfect approximation with the displayed isomorphism; its maps on cohomology remain isomorphisms above $m$ and surjections in degree $m$. The affine covers $W_{ac}$ and $U^{\prime}_{abc}$ and embeddings $i^{\prime}_{abc}$ now satisfy exactly [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] for $f^{\prime}$ and $E^{\prime}$. This proves the assertion for the fixed integer $m$.

source.place: Tag 09UR, final sentence invoking Cohomology Tag 09U7; Tag 09UI, clause (1).

proof.text: If $E$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$, then [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] says that it is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. Apply steps 1--4 separately to each $m$. The same definition gives pseudo-coherence of $Lq^*E$ relative to $S^{\prime}$; it does not require that the covers for different $m$ coincide.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09UR, lemma-base-change-relative-pseudo-coherent, specialized to flat base change; with perfect.tex Tag 0E23 and cohomology.tex Tag 09U7.
